readings: Level-sensitive D latch: q tracks d while ena is high (transparent), holds when ena is low, using always @(*) if (ena) q = d;
Edge-triggered D flip-flop: q samples d only on a clock/edge (e.g., always @(posedge ena)), so q changes one event later and never follows d continuously
ena is active-high: latch is transparent when ena == 1 and holds when ena == 0
ena is active-low: latch is transparent when ena == 0 and holds when ena == 1
q is undefined (X) from time 0 until the first enabling event, since no reset port or initial condition is specified
q must be initialized to a defined value (e.g., 0) at time 0 (initial block / declaration initializer)
Sensitivity covers d (always @(*) or always @(ena or d)): q updates combinationally in the same cycle as a change on d while ena is high
Sensitivity is always @(ena) only: changes on d while ena is high do not propagate to q until ena itself changes, giving a delayed/stale q
